agent_notes: The Hebrew has no 'but' after the doubled 'not to us'; KJV, ASV and Webster supply it, YLT and BBE too. I keep it in brackets in the literal layer. 'Chesed' is glossed 'covenant loyalty' (STEPBible) and 'faithfulness' for emet; the commentaries read 'al as 'for the sake of' (Radak: 'al odotekha), which is why the dramatic layer says 'for the sake of'.

'Yirei YHWH' is disputed: Rashi and Metzudat David take it as gentile God-fearers, Radak mainly as the wise within Israel (and mentions the other view), Meiri as a third class. I left the term as 'those who fear YHWH' and gave the range in the commentary without choosing.

Ibn Ezra reports R. Moshe's view ('our males' / 'the house of Israel = the females') and rejects it. I report it as his reported view only. The KJV's 'he will bless us' supplies an object the Hebrew lacks (first yevarekh has none); Webster brackets it.

STEPBible glosses laYahweh as 'by Yahweh'. I kept 'to YHWH' in the literal layer, since the lamed is the preposition itself, and used 'by' in the word gloss and the dramatic layer where it carries the sense of agent.

agent_notes: YLT renders the first two clauses without 'have' and skips the last clause, which it attaches to v.8 ('Nor do they mutter through their throat'); the Hebrew verse division puts 'they make no sound in their throat' in v.7, as I do. Yehgu is glossed 'make a sound' (STEPBible), literally 'murmur, mutter'; Radak, Meiri and Metzudat Zion all tie it to the cooing of Isaiah 38:14.

Kemohem yihyu is taken as a wish ('may they become like them'), as Ibn Ezra, Radak and Meiri say 'derekh tefillah'. KJV and ASV's 'are like' / 'shall be like' reads it as a statement or prediction; the literal layer keeps the Hebrew's neutral 'will be', the dramatic layer the imprecation.
